questions.def: Use present simple after 'as soon as' when referring to the future.
questions.question: I will call you as soon as I ___ home.

questions.def: Use past perfect for actions completed before another action in the past.
questions.question: She ___ the movie before she read the book.

questions.def: Use 'will' for future actions with time clauses.
questions.question: I ___ here until you arrive.

questions.def: Use past simple after 'before' when both actions are in the past.
questions.question: Before she went to bed, she ___ her teeth.

questions.def: Use past perfect 'by the time' to show completion before another past action.
questions.question: By the time we arrived, they ___ all the food.

questions.def: Future tense cannot be used in the main clause with a time clause.
questions.question: He will call you when he arrives tomorrow.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'as soon as' for future actions.
questions.question: I will leave as soon as I ___ this email.

questions.def: Use future perfect 'by the time' to show completion before a future action.
questions.question: We ___ dinner by the time you get here.

questions.def: Use past continuous for simultaneous actions in the past using 'while'.
questions.question: While I was cooking, he ___ the dishes.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'the moment' when referring to the future.
questions.question: I will call you the moment I ___.

questions.def: 'As long as' introduces a condition for a future result using 'will'.
questions.question: As long as you study hard, you ___ pass the exam.

questions.def: Use 'will' to describe future actions in 'if' clauses (type 1 conditional).
questions.question: I ___ to the party if I finish my work.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'until' when referring to the future.
questions.question: Until he ___, I will stay here.

questions.def: 'Whenever' implies a repeated action, so use present simple.
questions.question: Whenever I feel sad, I ___ to music.

questions.def: Use past continuous for an action in progress at a specific time in the past.
questions.question: The last time I saw her, she ___ a red dress.

questions.def: Use past simple after 'since' when talking about a past starting point.
questions.question: Since I ___ you last, I have been very busy.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'unless' to refer to the future.
questions.question: I will not go out unless it ___ raining.

questions.def: Use past continuous to describe a continuous action in the past.
questions.question: While she ___, I read a book.

questions.def: Use past perfect to show an action completed before another in the past.
questions.question: They ___ all the cake before I arrived.

questions.def: 'The moment' introduces a past action, so use past simple.
questions.question: The moment he arrived, everyone ___ silent.

questions.def: Use future simple after 'by the time' to indicate a future action.
questions.question: By the time she finishes, I ___ home.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'as soon as' when referring to the future.
questions.question: I will let you know as soon as I ___.

questions.def: Use past continuous to describe simultaneous actions in the past using 'while'.
questions.question: While he was studying, his brother ___ video games.

questions.def: Use past perfect continuous for duration before a past action.
questions.question: She ___ English for five years before she moved here.

questions.def: Use present simple after 'as soon as' when referring to the future.
questions.question: I will call you as soon as I ___ home.

questions.def: Use present simple in the time clause after 'before'.
questions.question: Before she ___ to work, she drinks coffee.

questions.def: Don't use 'will' in the time clause after 'after'.
questions.question: After he will finish his work, he will go out.

questions.def: 'After' requires present simple after the game is finished.
questions.question: We can go ___ dinner after we finish the game.

questions.def: Use past continuous after 'while' to describe two actions happening simultaneously.
questions.question: While I ___ cooking, he was cleaning.

questions.def: Use future simple in the main clause when there's a time clause.
questions.question: They ___ here until they find a new house.
